authority: Causeway Coast and Glens Borough Council
researched_by: Northern Ireland primary legislation on legislation.gov.uk, the council's own car park inventory PDF and committee papers, its caravan park pages and CampManager booking system, National Trust and nidirect pages for the non-council sites, and van-user listings for coordinates and signage
policy_summary:
The first Northern Ireland authority in this dataset, and it lands at the provision-heavy end of the whole UK spectrum. Causeway Coast and Glens owns and directly operates SEVEN holiday parks - including a purpose-built ten-bay motorhome aire with a service point at Portrush - and publishes NO council-wide rule against overnight parking or sleeping in a vehicle anywhere in its 59 car parks. On the most van-pressured stretch of coast in Northern Ireland, the council's answer has been to build somewhere to go rather than to ban.

Before anything else, the legal framework, because it is not the British one and everything later depends on getting it right. On 1 APRIL 2015 the Off-street Parking (Functions of District Councils) Act (Northern Ireland) 2015 (c. 3) transferred the Department's functions under Articles 10 to 14 and 25 to 27 of the Road Traffic Regulation (Northern Ireland) Order 1997 to the district councils, in relation to off-street parking places in their districts. 338 car parks moved to the 11 new councils. A new Article 9A defines 'the parking authority': the district council for off-street parking places, but the DEPARTMENT for park-and-ride and park-and-share places, and the DEPARTMENT for parking places on roads. So off-street is the council and ON-STREET REMAINS DfI ROADS - and DfI today operates only three charged car parks in all of Northern Ireland, the Belfast park-and-rides at Eastside, Northside and Great George's Street.

There is no Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 here and there are NO PSPOs - Part 4 of the Anti-social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014 does not extend to Northern Ireland. The council's car park instrument is an order under ARTICLE 13 of the 1997 Order, made under the Schedule 4 procedure, and the council uses exactly that language: its own public notice gives notice 'in accordance with The Road Traffic Regulation (Northern Ireland) Order 1997 (Schedule 4) as amended, to vary charges to Off Street Car Parks'. Enforcement is civil and decriminalised, under the Traffic Management (Northern Ireland) Order 2005: the council is the 'enforcement authority' for Article 14(1) offences in its off-street car parks, it employs TRAFFIC ATTENDANTS under Article 3 (not 'civil enforcement officers'), and they issue penalty charge notices under Articles 5 and 7 - white for off-street, buff for DfI's on-street.

And then the thing that changes the whole Northern Ireland picture. The OFF-STREET PARKING BYE-LAWS (NORTHERN IRELAND) 1996 (S.R. 1996 No. 237), made under Article 105(1) of the Road Traffic (Northern Ireland) Order 1981 and in operation since 1 July 1996, contain at bye-law 21: 'A person shall not use any part of a parking place or any vehicle left in a parking place - (a) for sleeping or camping purposes; (b) for eating or cooking purposes; or (c) for the purposes of servicing or washing any vehicle'. Bye-law 27 makes contravention a summary offence carrying a fine up to level 2. Bye-law 13 lets a vehicle contravening bye-law 21 be REMOVED. Northern Ireland has had a blanket statutory ban on sleeping in a vehicle in a public car park since 1996, twenty years before the first English PSPO - not by council choice, not site by site, but nationally and by default. Whether it still bites after 2015 is the open question of the whole Northern Ireland tier, and it is set out in the notes.

Against that, what this council actually does. It runs seven holiday parks in-house, all bookable through one CampManager portal, all with council wardens on council email addresses, none leased out: Sandhill Drive motorhome park at Portrush, Carrick Dhu at Portrush, Juniper Hill at Portstewart, Benone near Limavady, Drumaheglis marina at Ballymoney, and Cushendall and Cushendun on the Antrim coast. Sandhill Drive is the one that matters most - ten motorhome bays and two service bays, pay and display, first come first served with no booking, a token-operated aire de service with fresh water, grey drain, leisure battery charging and a dedicated chemical sluice, reported at 50p an hour or GBP 12 for 24 hours. It is a genuine aire, run by a council, on the Causeway Coast. It is also reported as partly out of service.

The council's tightening is about money rather than nights. Seasonal charges of 50p an hour, 1 April to 30 September, arrived in 2025 at Ballycastle Harbour, Ballycastle Marina and Portrush West Bay; the first season returned GBP 166,739 against GBP 27,617 of enforcement cost. Portrush Harbour Road charges GBP 1.00 an hour until 21:30, the latest cut-off in the borough. And the council has a second lever it has begun to use: redesignating a car park as PRIVATE LAND, which takes it outside the statutory PCN regime and allows a GBP 90 parking charge notice, halved to GBP 45 within 14 days. That was done at Portrush East Strand and proposed for Ballintoy Harbour in December 2021. Where a hard overnight ban does exist on this coast it almost always belongs to somebody else - the National Trust, the Forest Service, or a 2.2 metre height barrier.
notes:
THIS IS THE FIRST NORTHERN IRELAND FILE. The framework below is meant to be reused, and later NI authorities should cite it rather than re-deriving it.

SCHEMA MAPPING FOR NORTHERN IRELAND. The instrument vocabulary was built for Great Britain and has no NI-specific values, so fix the mapping now and keep it:
- 'off_street_parking_order' in an NI file means an order under ARTICLE 13 of the Road Traffic Regulation (Northern Ireland) Order 1997, made under the Schedule 4 procedure by the council as 'parking authority' under the new Article 9A. It does NOT mean a Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 s.32/35 order, which has no application in Northern Ireland.
- 'on_street_tro' in an NI file means a Department for Infrastructure order, never a council one. On-street is DfI Roads throughout Northern Ireland.
- 'pspo' MUST NEVER APPEAR IN AN NI FILE. Part 4 of the Anti-social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014 extends to England and Wales only. If you find yourself reaching for it, the answer you want is byelaws.
- 'byelaw' in an NI car park context will usually mean the Off-Street Parking Bye-Laws (Northern Ireland) 1996 (S.R. 1996 No. 237) rather than anything the council made itself.

THE 1996 BYELAWS ARE THE LOAD-BEARING UNCERTAINTY AND MUST BE FLAGGED IN EVERY NI FILE. Bye-law 21 prohibits using a parking place or a vehicle left in one 'for sleeping or camping purposes'; bye-law 27 makes that a summary offence with a fine up to level 2; bye-law 13 authorises removal of a vehicle contravening it. On its face that is a Northern Ireland-wide sleeping ban in every public car park, in force since 1 July 1996. BUT the byelaws were made by the Department under Article 105(1) of the Road Traffic (Northern Ireland) Order 1981, and they refer throughout to 'the Department'. The 2015 Act transferred functions under the 1997 Order and the 2005 Order - it did NOT on its face transfer byelaw functions under the 1981 Order. So whether the 1996 byelaws still bite in a council car park after 1 April 2015, and whether any council has made replacement byelaws under section 90 of the Local Government Act (Northern Ireland) 1972, is UNRESOLVED. Until somebody resolves it, every NI record that relies on bye-law 21 should carry status 'unknown' and medium confidence at best. Note also that the byelaws are conduct-based, not vehicle-class-based: they say nothing about caravans or motor caravans. A motorhome PARKED is lawful; a motorhome SLEPT IN is the offence. That is the opposite emphasis from most English PSPOs, which name the vehicle.

TWO PENALTY ROUTES, AND THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE. A parking-order contravention - no ticket, overstay, wrong bay - is a CIVIL penalty charge notice under Articles 5 and 7 of the Traffic Management (NI) Order 2005, issued by council traffic attendants. A byelaw contravention - sleeping, camping, cooking, fires, alcohol - is a CRIMINAL summary offence prosecuted under bye-law 27, or in practice a removal under bye-law 13. A motorhome asleep in a properly paid bay has not committed a PCN offence at all. Anyone modelling NI enforcement as 'like a PCN for overnight parking' has it wrong.

WHERE THE NI COUNCIL PARKING ORDERS ACTUALLY LIVE - a research warning that will save the next eight files. The old departmental instrument, the Off-Street Parking Order (Northern Ireland) 2000 (S.R. 2000 No. 384), was to be repealed and each council asked to make 'its equivalent to the Off-Street Parking Order'. The Department's letter to council chief executives calls these draft ADMINISTRATIVE orders. They do not appear on legislation.gov.uk. DO NOT CONCLUDE FROM A NIL RESULT ON LEGISLATION.GOV.UK THAT AN NI COUNCIL HAS NO PARKING ORDER - it will be a local instrument, obtainable from the council or from its public notices, and Causeway Coast and Glens' own notice of 15 August 2016 proves it uses the Schedule 4 procedure to vary charges.

AND DO NOT LOOK FOR LEGACY DISTRICT COUNCIL PARKING ORDERS. Before 2015 the eleven legacy councils in this area - Coleraine, Moyle, Limavady, Ballymoney here - had NO off-street car park function at all. The car parks were the Department's, run under the 2000 Order. There is therefore no inherited Coleraine or Moyle car parking order to find. Any surviving legacy instrument will be a foreshore, beach or amenity byelaw, not a parking one. This is the reverse of the English pattern, where district-council orders and campsites survive reorganisation and are the messiest category.

WHAT IS NOT THIS COUNCIL'S - name them so nobody researches them twice under this slug. GIANT'S CAUSEWAY visitor centre car park is NATIONAL TRUST, bundled into the Visitor Experience ticket, car park hours 05:00-20:00, and the Trust's own booking page says overnight parking is not permitted; its overflow at Innisfree Farm, 60 Causeway Road, is GBP 12 via JustPark with the same explicit no-overnight rule. CARRICK-A-REDE is National Trust, parking included in the rope bridge ticket, car park closing 18:30. WHITEPARK BAY is National Trust, free, stated as open all day, no published overnight rule and no barrier - materially the loosest of the Trust sites. PORTSTEWART STRAND is National Trust, GBP 8.50 per vehicle card only, cars driven onto and parked on the beach, car park 10:00-18:00 with a hard beach-clearing time; no overnight rule is published because the clearing time makes one unnecessary. CUSHENDUN VILLAGE is National Trust, with two free dawn-to-dusk car parks at the Corner House and Glenmona House, and van users report 'no overnight parking' signage on the quayside. All of those belong in national-trust.json. GLENARIFF FOREST PARK is FOREST SERVICE NI / DAERA, not the council - entry charges, gates locked at dusk, and a caravan site that is PIN-code gated so an unbooked arrival physically cannot get in; it books through nidirect.campmanager.com, a different portal from the council's. FAIR HEAD is privately owned by the McBride family with a GBP 3 honesty box. The private caravan parks in the borough are Portballintrae, Watertop Farm, Causeway Coast Holiday Park (Hagans Leisure), Fairhead, Glenmore, Ballyness, Bush, Tullans, Maddybenny, Golden Sands, Highview, Bellemont, Ballymacrea and Hilltop - private supply, not council. There is no Haven or Parkdean park in this borough.

THE ON-STREET TRAP AT PORTRUSH. Van users report signage on the angled bays at Ramore Avenue reading 'Mon-Sun midnight-09:00, 1 hour, no return within 1 hour' - a restriction that exists purely to defeat overnight parking, timed to run through the night only. It is ON-STREET, so it is a Department for Infrastructure order and NOT this council's, and it is deliberately not recorded here. It is also the clearest evidence in Northern Ireland that somebody is legislating against sleeping in vehicles - just not the council. THE DATASET NEEDS A 'DEPARTMENT FOR INFRASTRUCTURE (ROADS)' AUTHORITY FILE, and it will be a large one: DfI holds every on-street restriction in Northern Ireland and every layby on the A2 Antrim Coast Road and the Causeway Coastal Route.

ENFORCEMENT REALITY. Pre-2016 the departmental contracts were NSL for enforcement, around 75 full-time equivalents across NI for off-street, and Spur Information Solutions for PCN processing; both broke in October 2016 and councils chose between in-house teams and buying Transport NI services. Who patrols Causeway Coast and Glens' car parks in 2026 is unconfirmed. What is confirmed is that the council's 2025 seasonal charging cost GBP 27,617 to enforce against GBP 166,739 of income - so there IS a patrol, it is funded, and it is out in the season.

DIRECTION OF TRAVEL. Provision is stable and mature; the movement is all on the charging side - free car parks becoming seasonally charged, and free car parks becoming 'private land' with GBP 90 charge notices. Neither is aimed at motorhomes. But the private-land designation is the mechanism that would let this council impose an overnight condition without any order, byelaw or consultation at all, and Ballintoy is where it would happen first.
open_questions: ARE THE OFF-STREET PARKING BYE-LAWS (NI) 1996 STILL IN FORCE, AND DO THEY APPLY IN COUNCIL CAR PARKS AFTER 1 APRIL 2015? This is the single most important unresolved question in the Northern Ireland tier. The 'Changes to legislation' record on legislation.gov.uk could not be loaded, and the 2015 Act does not on its face transfer byelaw functions under Article 105 of the Road Traffic (NI) Order 1981.
Has Causeway Coast and Glens, or any NI council, made replacement car park byelaws under section 90 of the Local Government Act (Northern Ireland) 1972?
What is the exact title and date of Causeway Coast and Glens' own off-street parking order? It is an administrative order, not a Statutory Rule, so it must come from the council direct.
A citation confirming that Part 4 of the Anti-social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014 does not extend to Northern Ireland. Stated here as settled law but not evidenced in this session.

Do the Unauthorised Encampments (Northern Ireland) Order 2005 or the Clean Neighbourhoods and Environment Act (Northern Ireland) 2011 give a council anything usable against overnight vehicles in a car park? Neither was researched.

Nightly tariffs for five of the seven council holiday parks. The council publishes no rate table; prices only appear inside the CampManager booking flow. Only Carrick Dhu (GBP 33-36) and Juniper Hill (about GBP 28) could be sourced, and both from third parties.
Is there a maximum stay at any of the seven council parks, or at Sandhill Drive? None is published anywhere.

Are the Sandhill Drive aire de service machine and chemical sluice back in working order? The council's tourism listing says they are 'not functioning at present', which if true means the only chemical disposal in the borough's public provision is out of use.
Is Sandhill Drive open all year? No seasonal closure is published, unlike the seven holiday parks which all shut for winter.
Cushendall Holiday Park pitch count: the tourism site says 34 touring plus 6 tent, the live booking system says 14 fully serviced touring pitches. One of them is out of date.

Was Ballintoy Harbour car park actually redesignated as private land after the December 2021 committee paper, and was the 50p an hour tariff introduced? The council's own car park PDF still lists it as free.

Coordinates for Ballintoy Harbour car park, Drumaheglis, Portstewart Strand and Murlough Bay could not be corroborated from any citable source and are deliberately left null or approximated from a postcode. Do not fill them in by inference.
Who owns Torr Head and Murlough Bay, and is there any rule at either? Nothing published was found, which on that coast probably means the restriction is the road rather than the law.

sites.name: Sandhill Drive Motorhome Park and Aire de Service, Portrush
sites.price_note: Reported as GBP 0.50 an hour or GBP 12.00 for 24 hours. The council page says only 'hourly rates for day and overnight parking' - the GBP 12 figure is third-party and unconfirmed.
sites.payment_notes: The council page says cash or card; the council's own tourism listing says cash only. Service tokens are GBP 2.00-2.50 and are sold OFF SITE, at Hillcrest Service Station and Portrush Filling Station - buy them before you arrive.
prohibits: no electric hook-up at the bays
sites.notes: THE BEST SINGLE FINDING IN THE FILE AND THE ONE THE PARKING PAGES DO NOT MENTION - it sits under the council's caravan parks section, not its parking section. A purpose-built council aire: ten motorhome bays plus two service bays, pay and display, FIRST COME FIRST SERVED WITH NO ADVANCE BOOKING, which makes it the only genuinely turn-up-and-stay council provision on the north coast. Motorhomes only. The token-operated service point takes GBP 2 to GBP 2.50 for either 1kW of electricity or 100 litres of water. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the council's own tourism listing states the aire machine and the chemical sluice are 'not functioning at present' - verify before relying on the sluice, because it is the only public chemical disposal in the borough. If the ten bays are full the park office will place you at Carrick Dhu or Juniper Hill by arrangement. Telephone 028 7082 3333. Separate from, and adjacent to, the free 139-space Sandhill Drive (Fire Station) council car park.

sites.name: All Causeway Coast and Glens Borough Council off-street car parks - sleeping and camping
sites.notes:
THE ESTATE-WIDE RECORD FOR NORTHERN IRELAND, AND IT IS A STATUTE RATHER THAN A COUNCIL DECISION. The Off-Street Parking Bye-Laws (Northern Ireland) 1996 (S.R. 1996 No. 237), made under Article 105(1) of the Road Traffic (Northern Ireland) Order 1981 and in operation since 1 July 1996, provide at bye-law 21 that 'a person shall not use any part of a parking place or any vehicle left in a parking place - (a) for sleeping or camping purposes; (b) for eating or cooking purposes; or (c) for the purposes of servicing or washing any vehicle'. Bye-law 27: summary conviction, fine not exceeding level 2. Bye-law 13: a vehicle contravening bye-law 21 may be REMOVED. Bye-law 25 additionally forbids erecting structures without consent and lighting fires; bye-law 23 forbids drinking alcohol in a designated car park; bye-law 11 requires the engine stopped; bye-law 19 forbids loud noise.

Status is 'unknown' DELIBERATELY. The byelaws refer throughout to 'the Department', and the 2015 transfer covered functions under the 1997 and 2005 Orders, not byelaw functions under the 1981 Order. Whether they still apply in a council car park after 1 April 2015 is unresolved and is the biggest open question in the Northern Ireland tier. Enforcement is recorded as 'fpn' for want of a better value: the real route is summary PROSECUTION under bye-law 27 or removal under bye-law 13, NOT a penalty charge notice - a PCN cannot be issued for sleeping, only for a parking-order contravention.

The council itself publishes nothing about overnight parking, sleeping or motorhomes: not on its parking pages, not in its 59-car-park inventory PDF, and not in its January 2026 committee report on seasonal charging, which does not mention motorhomes at all. If a rule bites here, it is this one, and it is not the council's.

sites.name: Whiterocks Beach car park, Portrush
sites.search_hint: Whiterocks Beach car park, 111 Dunluce Road, Portrush
sites.notes: The clearest signed no-overnight rule on any council land in the borough: van users consistently report signage reading 'No overnight parking or camping - daytime parking only'. Free, only ten to twelve spaces, with council toilets and showers. Reported as THE ONLY ONE OF THE PORTRUSH COASTAL CAR PARKS WITHOUT A HEIGHT RESTRICTION, which is why it attracts vans and why it is the one that got signed. Enforcement is reported as inconsistent. Instrument left 'unknown' rather than guessed: the sign could be the council relying on bye-law 21 of the 1996 byelaws, or a bare landowner's notice, and the difference decides whether ignoring it is an offence or a trespass. No wording could be sourced from the council itself.
sites.geocode_precision: the beach car park at 111 Dunluce Road, from a van-user listing that names the signage

sites.name: Portrush East Strand car park
sites.search_hint: East Strand car park, The Links, Portrush
sites.notes: The borough's biggest car park at 537 spaces, and the case that shows how this council actually restricts. TWO SEPARATE MECHANISMS OPERATE HERE AND NEITHER MENTIONS THE NIGHT. First, a 2.2 METRE HEIGHT BARRIER, now reported as enforced - that is the effective motorhome exclusion, and it is engineering rather than law. Second, East Strand has been REDESIGNATED AS A 'PRIVATE LAND' CAR PARK, taking it outside the statutory penalty charge regime and allowing a GBP 90 parking charge notice reduced to GBP 45 within 14 days. That designation is the precedent the December 2021 committee paper proposed to follow at Ballintoy. Van users report no signage restricting overnight parking as such, and daytime charging of about 30p an hour or GBP 2.60 a day. applies_to is recorded as over_length because the height barrier, not any rule about sleeping, is what actually stops a motorhome.
sites.geocode_precision: the beachside parking at 49 The Links on the East Strand, from a van-user listing that records the height barrier

sites.name: Ballintoy Harbour car park
sites.search_hint: Ballintoy Harbour car park, Harbour Road, Ballintoy
sites.notes: The pressure point to watch on this coast, and the one place the council has actively moved on. 46 spaces, still listed as FREE in the council's own car park inventory. A December 2021 Environmental Services committee paper proposed redesignating Harbour Road car park as a 'PRIVATE LAND' car park - the same status as Portrush East Strand - specifically to allow enforcement patrols and PARKING CHARGE NOTICES AT GBP 90, halved to GBP 45 if paid within 14 days, alongside a 50p an hour tariff Monday to Sunday 08:30-18:30 projected to raise about GBP 35,282 a year. The paper is aimed at 'trailers and other inappropriate parking' and DOES NOT MENTION OVERNIGHT PARKING OR CAMPING AT ALL - but private-land designation is precisely the lever that would let the council impose an overnight condition without any order or byelaw. Status recorded as draft because it could not be confirmed whether the redesignation and tariff were implemented. Pressure here is real: police were reported to have run out of parking tickets at Ballintoy Harbour during a heatwave. The single-track harbour road is a poor motorhome proposition regardless. NO COORDINATE IS RECORDED - none could be corroborated from a citable source. A free signed lay-by two kilometres away at 144 Whitepark Road (about 55.2301, -6.3926) is widely used overnight with no reported restriction, but it is a roadside lay-by and therefore DfI Roads, not this council.

sites.name: Ballycastle Harbour, Ballycastle Marina and Portrush West Bay - seasonal charging
sites.price_note: 50p an hour, 1 April to 30 September, Monday to Sunday.
sites.notes: The council's live direction of travel, introduced in 2025 at three previously free car parks: Ballycastle Harbour, Ballycastle Marina and Portrush West Bay (West Strand, 186 spaces). The first season returned GBP 166,739 of income against GBP 27,617 of enforcement cost and came in GBP 80,878 under budget - so it is working, it is patrolled, and it will spread. Rathlin residents and workers and Ballycastle Marina boat owners get permits. The committee report reviewing the first season DOES NOT MENTION MOTORHOMES, OVERNIGHT PARKING OR CAMPING ANYWHERE - this is a revenue measure, not a van measure. Recorded without coordinates because it covers three separate car parks in two towns. The charging window ends at 18:30, so nothing here bites on the night; the effect on a van is that the free coastal car parks it used to rely on now cost money by day.

sites.name: Downhill Beach and Benone Strand
sites.search_hint: Benone Strand and Downhill Beach, Seacoast Road, Limavady
sites.notes: RECORDED BECAUSE OF WHAT IS ABSENT. Both beaches are managed by the council, both have FREE parking at the entrance and FREE PARKING ON THE BEACH ITSELF, Downhill explicitly year-round, and NO overnight or camping restriction is published for either. Seven miles of Blue Flag sand on which the council invites you to park a vehicle for nothing is, on the published evidence, the least restricted overnight ground in the borough - which is exactly why the position needs checking on the ground before anyone relies on it. The real constraints are physical and seasonal, not legal: vehicle access is restricted by soft wind-blown sand and is periodically suspended by advisory notice, the area to the right of the wooden posts at the Downhill entrance is closed to vehicles, access on to Magilligan Point may be closed when the MOD firing range is operating, dogs are restricted 1 June to 15 September and horse riding 1 May to 30 September. Downhill Demesne above the beach is National Trust, but the beach car park is the council's. Status is unknown and confidence low because the absence of a rule is not the same as permission - and if the 1996 byelaws apply, bye-law 21 applies here too.
